classification.contract: Repair the cache so a fresh online-mode query whose observer mounts and unmounts entirely offline does not later call its signal-consuming query function with a live signal after reconnect, regardless of refetchOnReconnect. Preserve supported behavior: multiple observers can share a fetch; unconsumed active work may finish into the cache after its observer leaves; consumed work can be aborted; cancellation restores prior query data and status and settles its originating attempt; late completion cannot publish as a newer attempt. Keep the supported query interfaces, dependencies, and build/test configuration. Change product source only. The reported defect constrains the offline-unmounted query's post-reconnect invocation; it does not establish a general ban on post-reconnect queries.

unknowns: The source does not establish that every paused, unstarted attempt must be physically aborted, nor that every post-reconnect query invocation is prohibited.
The exact settlement mechanism for an offline-unmounted, never-invoked attempt is not specified by the task.

findings.judgment: Execution-agent AI-assisted task/source review, not independent human approval or an additional model judge. No scoring/trajectory/reference patch was used.

The new Contract explicitly preserves WITH A LIVE SIGNAL inside the prohibited invocation event under fresh-online/offline-mount-departure conditions. It does not impose zero invocation or prohibit valid post-reconnect activity generally.

No entry or entry with an already-aborted signal remains compatible with the actual Contract. The exact disposition of never-invoked work is accurately left unspecified; no requirement to settle/abort every unstarted or paused attempt is fabricated.

README 12-16 documents multi-observer shared work, unconsumed active background completion, consumed-flight abort, cancellation revert/settlement and late-completion separation. Contract preserves all without turning view departure into universal cancellation.

Current unsubscribe branches on the shared query consumed marker, as the source-fact claim correctly states. Attempt-local controller/completion identity does not require migrating that shared record. The reported-defect/requirement owner labels denote the originating attempt rather than record storage location.
T4 and the five required shared/cache/observer/attempt/lazy-read/async-resume mechanisms are supported by current docs and source; no case/cluster/history is used as routing evidence.

No general before-return persistence boundary, blanket abort of paused work or all-invocation ban is established. These remain non-required scope/implementation unknowns, not assumptions used for admission.

One reported-defect statement ends with a dangling regardless colon under its compact output limit. The complete Contract and requirement claim both retain independence from the refetch option and the live-signal qualifier, so this raw formatting defect adds no contrary requirement. Nothing is completed or rewritten by Python.
